page: Microsoft Azure B16ps_v2 is a burstable virtual machine belonging to the Bpsv2 server family. It is powered by an arm64 architecture featuring an Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor. This processor provides 16 physical cores and 16 vCPUs, operating at a clock speed of 3.0 GHz with no hyperthreading. The CPU cache configuration includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This server does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable, relying on remote storage volumes for data persistence.

Benchmark evaluations place the B16ps_v2 in the average performance tier for most multi-core and memory operations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU test yielded a score of 28877.71, while the single-core performance reached 1822.49. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrated read speeds of 1126.93 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 130.2 GB/sec for larger uncached blocks, alongside a write speed of 67.46 GB/sec. The server shows average capabilities in software compilation with Clang (16770.0) and database operations (11297.67). However, it exhibits weaker performance in single-threaded bzip3 decompression, text processing, and cryptographic operations, as evidenced by a Passmark CPU encryption score of 2608.59.

Given its burstable CPU allocation model, the B16ps_v2 offers a cost-efficient profile for workloads with variable resource demands. It is well-suited for environments that experience intermittent spikes in activity rather than continuous high-utilization states. Appropriate workloads include static web serving, where it achieves a throughput of 18.84 GB/sec, Redis caching layers with a measured 21.22 million SET operations per second, and general-purpose application hosting. It is less suitable for sustained high-performance computing, intensive cryptographic tasks, or large-scale LLM inference due to its burstable CPU limits and weaker single-threaded performance.
